items.title: Canada Fires Back in Trade War Against Trump With Up to 50% Tariffs
items.summary: Canada said the higher levies, on items from aluminum foil to dishwashers to fish, would help protect workers, producers and manufacturers harmed by new Trump tariffs.

items.title: Iran May Have Little to Lose as U.S. Tries to Squeeze Its Economy
items.summary: Experts warn that a campaign aimed at avoiding military escalation could instead provoke it, as Iranian leaders vow retaliation across the oil-rich Gulf.

items.title: Christian Convert Who Fled Iran and Was Deported By Trump Finds New Home
items.summary: Artemis Ghasemzadeh, who had escaped religious persecution, was deported to Panama under Trump’s immigration crackdown. Now, Canada has given her asylum.

items.title: What Happened to the Coveted Western Tanks Sent to Ukraine?
items.summary: Ukraine pleaded for the expensive weapons, and ultimately got them, but drones have rendered them almost unusable.

items.title: Israeli Lawmaker Smashes Palestinian Monument in West Bank
items.summary: Videos showed Israeli troops standing by as Zvi Sukkot attacked the monument with a sledgehammer. The military said soldiers had stopped the demolition.

items.title: Dozens Massacred in Haiti, Officials Say, Heightening Fears of Gangs
items.summary: Gangs targeted a key community on the outskirts of the capital, raising fears about the gangs’ next move. The mayor said at least 25 people had been killed, but the U.N. put the death toll at 47.

items.title: India’s Summer of Youth Protests Is Boiling Over
items.summary: The police fired water cannons at protesters in the state of Bihar, while the leaders of the ‘Cockroach’ student movement vowed to return to Delhi’s streets.

items.title: How U.S.-Canada Tariff Negotiations Turned Into an All-Out Trade War
items.summary: Detailed accounts of the final hours of the negotiations show that, while the United States offered Canada what it said was the best deal of any country, what Canada had to give up in exchange was seen as unthinkable.

items.title: Tornado Rips Through Towns in Southern France
items.summary: An uncommonly powerful tornado destroyed dozens of homes and knocked out power to about 2,800 households.

items.title: U.S. Removes Syria From Its List of Terrorism Sponsors
items.summary: The move lifted economic sanctions on the country, raising hopes of further recovery after its brutal civil war.

items.title: SpaceX to Spend $100 Billion on New Spaceport in Louisiana
items.summary: It would be the rocket company’s second private launch site after Starbase, its headquarters in South Texas.

items.title: E.P.A. Moves to Curb Public Input on Air Pollution Permits for Data Centers
items.summary: Under the proposal, states would no longer need to provide public notice or solicit comments on air pollution permits for data centers and other projects.

items.title: Trump’s Canada Tariffs Rely on Untested Law
items.summary: The president has invoked a long dormant section of law to hit one of America’s closest allies, a move that has troubled courts in the past.

items.title: China Pushes Back After Trump Tightens the Screws on Iran
items.summary: The Trump administration risks a clash with Beijing as it tries to cut off Iran’s economic lifelines without upending a fragile U.S.-China truce.

items.title: The Heat on Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Grows
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s plans to intervene in bond markets have drawn widespread criticism, including from a prominent former mentor.

items.title: This A.I. Start-Up Aims to Reverse the Backlash Against Data Centers
items.summary: Emerald AI, now valued at $1.05 billion, uses software to keep power demand at the computing facilities from getting out of control.

items.title: Target Apologizes and Drops Halloween Costume Criticized as Racist
items.summary: The children’s costume evoked blackface imagery, critics said. “We know we got this wrong, and we are deeply sorry,” the retailer said in response.

items.title: Is It Time for This 95-Year-Old Pianist to Retire?
items.summary: Her vision and hearing are deteriorating, but she still wants to feel like she’s on top.

items.title: Many N.F.L. Players Get Brain Disease. Why Hasn’t OSHA Intervened?
items.summary: “We never see things that are this dire,” a former chief scientist of the agency said about rates of C.T.E. in former players.

items.title: U.S. Tariffs Could Price Canadian Firms Out of U.S. and Threaten Thousands of Jobs
items.summary: The 50 percent tariffs President Trump imposed on Canadian exports to the United States will make it impossible for many Canadian companies to continue to sell to the U.S. market, economists say.

items.title: Why Irregular’s A.I. Tests for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI Went Off the Rails
items.summary: Irregular, an Israeli start-up, worked with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to assess the security of their A.I. models. It made a mistake. Then the tests went off the rails.

items.title: After Hugging Face Was Attacked By A.I. Agents, It Embarked on a Crusade
items.summary: Hugging Face, a start-up that was breached by rogue bots from OpenAI, is using the hack to push for openness in A.I. development.

items.title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
items.summary: Companies like Google and Microsoft have used their money, their might and their massive reach to influence nearly every step of the education supply chain.

items.title: Laptop Fire on American Airlines Flight Injures at Least One Passenger
items.summary: Flight attendants used a fireproof bag to contain the computer after its lithium battery began smoking. One passenger was treated on the ground for injuries.

items.title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has.
items.summary: The mysterious collapse of a European cryptocurrency exchange helps to explain why the industry hasn’t shaken off its reputation as a magnet for criminals.

items.title: What if Your Texts Traveled as Slowly as a Carrier Pigeon?
items.summary: Apps that let users send digital messages at ultraslow speeds have taken off, with users reveling in a slower pace of life. (Just don’t use the them to make dinner plans.)

items.title: Anthropic Could Aim to Raise $100 Billion in Blockbuster I.P.O.
items.summary: The offering could value the five-year-old A.I. start-up at $2 trillion, its bankers have told potential investors, which would exceed Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

items.title: TikTok Settles With U.S. Over Child Privacy Concerns for $400 Million
items.summary: The Justice Department resolved a lawsuit that accused the social media company of illegally gathering children’s information.
